reconstructed_theorem_text: E_n=EuclideanSpace R (Fin(n+1)), the real (n+1)-coordinate space with its l2 Euclidean norm. Let S_n={z in E_n: ||z||=1}, considered as a subtype when it is used as a carrier. Let C_(n,N)=Fin N -> S_n. For a function a:S_n -> A into a type with a distinguished zero, write R(a)(z)=0 if z=0 and R(a)(z)=a(z/||z||) otherwise; normalization is the first component of the supplied H. For a:S_n->R and x:S_n, let Q(a,x)=P_(x-perp)(gradient_R R(a)(x)), where P_(x-perp) is starProjection onto the orthogonal complement of the real span of x. The supplied projection formulas make this b-<x,b>x for b=gradient_R R(a)(x). Here gradient_R h(x) is exactly the inverse Riesz map applied to fderiv_R h x. For arbitrary f:C_(n,N)->R, i:Fin N and x:C_(n,N), define f_(i,x)(y)=f(update x i y), where update changes only the ith coordinate. The target value is Q(f_(i,x),x_i). Thus the other coordinates stay fixed, the scalar slice is radially extended into E_n, and its ambient gradient at x_i is projected onto x_i-perp. There is no differentiability assumption or separate intrinsic-gradient theorem in this definition.
objects: A configuration scalar f, one factor index i, configuration x and the corresponding projected slice-gradient vector.
domains: n,N:Nat; f:C_(n,N)->R; i:Fin N; x:C_(n,N); output E_n.
quantifiers: Implicit n,N, followed by f, i, x.
assumptions: No regularity or integrability premise. i:Fin N supplies a valid index; none exists when N=0.
conclusion: Defined value object_9(y -> f(update x i y))(x i), expanded as projected radial-slice ambient gradient.
scopes: Pointwise partial-coordinate construction holding all other coordinates fixed; not a sum over factors.
constant_dependencies: One selected factor i, unit sphere radius, no 1/N or other multiplier.
